review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

10:1.sourceText: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ μὴ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τῶν προβάτων ἀλλὰ ἀναβαίνων ἀλλαχόθεν, ἐκεῖνος κλέπτης ἐστὶν καὶ λῃστής·
10:1.targetText: “Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ … εἰσερχόμενος ("the one entering") form one unit.
αὐλὴν τῶν προβάτων ("fold of the sheep") is rendered as one English word.

unmappedSource.reason: English "enter" takes the sheepfold as its object; εἰς ("into") is not separately expressed.
The resumptive ἐκεῖνος ("that one") is not rendered; whoever is the subject of is.

10:2.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας ποιμήν ἐστιν τῶν προβάτων.
10:2.targetText: But the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ … εἰσερχόμενος form one unit.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes "shepherd" definite; ποιμήν has no article.

10:3.sourceText: τούτῳ ὁ θυρωρὸς ἀνοίγει, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ τὰ ἴδια πρόβατα φωνεῖ κατ’ ὄνομα καὶ ἐξάγει αὐτά.
10:3.targetText: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen for his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of opens; ἀνοίγει has none.

10:4.sourceText: ὅταν τὰ ἴδια πάντα ἐκβάλῃ, ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν πορεύεται, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα αὐτῷ ἀκολουθεῖ, ὅτι οἴδασιν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ·
10:4.targetText: When he has brought out all his own, he goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

10:5.sourceText: ἀλλοτρίῳ δὲ οὐ μὴ ἀκολουθήσουσιν, ἀλλὰ φεύξονται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασιν τῶν ἀλλοτρίων τὴν φωνήν.
10:5.targetText: But they will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice.”

groups.note: τῶν ἀλλοτρίων ("of the strangers") is rendered his, pointing back to the stranger.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

10:6.sourceText: Ταύτην τὴν παροιμίαν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τίνα ἦν ἃ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς.
10:6.targetText: Jesus spoke to them using this illustration, but they did not understand what He was telling them.

groups.note: τίνα ἦν ἅ ("what the things were that") is condensed to what.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies "using"; in the Greek παροιμίαν is the direct object of εἶπεν ("spoke this illustration").

10:7.sourceText: Εἶπεν οὖν πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα τῶν προβάτων.
10:7.targetText: So He said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep.

groups.note: BSB renders the name Ἰησοῦς ("Jesus") as He here.
The genitive τῶν προβάτων ("of the sheep") is rendered for the sheep.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

10:8.sourceText: πάντες ὅσοι ἦλθον πρὸ ἐμοῦ κλέπται εἰσὶν καὶ λῃσταί· ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἤκουσαν αὐτῶν τὰ πρόβατα.
10:8.targetText: All who came before Me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.

groups.note: The present εἰσίν ("are") is rendered were.

10:9.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα· δι’ ἐμοῦ ἐάν τις εἰσέλθῃ, σωθήσεται, καὶ εἰσελεύσεται καὶ ἐξελεύσεται καὶ νομὴν εὑρήσει.
10:9.targetText: I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

10:10.sourceText: ὁ κλέπτης οὐκ ἔρχεται εἰ μὴ ἵνα κλέψῃ καὶ θύσῃ καὶ ἀπολέσῃ· ἐγὼ ἦλθον ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχωσιν καὶ περισσὸν ἔχωσιν.
10:10.targetText: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.

groups.note: οὐκ … εἰ μή ("not … except") is rendered only.
περισσόν ("abundance") is rendered in all its fullness.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies "it" (life) as the object; the Greek object is περισσόν.

10:11.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός. ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλὸς τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ τίθησιν ὑπὲρ τῶν προβάτων·
10:11.targetText: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article of the attributive adjective has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

10:12.sourceText: ὁ μισθωτὸς καὶ οὐκ ὢν ποιμήν, οὗ οὐκ ἔστιν τὰ πρόβατα ἴδια, θεωρεῖ τὸν λύκον ἐρχόμενον καὶ ἀφίησιν τὰ πρόβατα καὶ φεύγει,— καὶ ὁ λύκος ἁρπάζει αὐτὰ καὶ σκορπίζει·—
10:12.targetText: The hired hand is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock.

groups.note: The participle ὤν ("being") becomes the main verb is.
The relative οὗ ("whose") is rendered and … his, as a new clause.
BSB turns the first of the καί-joined clauses into a When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes "not being a shepherd" a separate statement; καί ("and") is not rendered there.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes "shepherd" definite; ποιμήν has no article.
English supplies the object of scatters; σκορπίζει has none.

10:13.sourceText: ὅτι μισθωτός ἐστιν καὶ οὐ μέλει αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν προβάτων.
10:13.targetText: The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep.

groups.note: οὐ μέλει αὐτῷ ("it is no concern to him") is rendered is unconcerned.

unmappedTarget.reason: English restates "runs away" from the previous verse; the Greek verse begins with ὅτι ("because").

10:14.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, καὶ γινώσκω τὰ ἐμὰ καὶ γινώσκουσί με τὰ ἐμά,
10:14.targetText: I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me,

groups.note: τὰ ἐμά ("My own") is rendered My sheep.
τὰ ἐμά ("My own") is rendered My sheep.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article of the attributive adjective has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

10:15.sourceText: καθὼς γινώσκει με ὁ Πατὴρ κἀγὼ γινώσκω τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ τὴν ψυχήν μου τίθημι ὑπὲρ τῶν προβάτων.
10:15.targetText: just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father. And I lay down My life for the sheep.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

10:16.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλα πρόβατα ἔχω ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης· κἀκεῖνα δεῖ με ἀγαγεῖν, καὶ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσουσιν, καὶ γενήσεται μία ποίμνη, εἷς ποιμήν.
10:16.targetText: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.

groups.note: κἀκεῖνα ("those also"): ἐκεῖνα = them, καί = as well.
Same verb, in another form in BSB's Greek text.

10:17.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτό με ὁ Πατὴρ ἀγαπᾷ ὅτι ἐγὼ τίθημι τὴν ψυχήν μου, ἵνα πάλιν λάβω αὐτήν.
10:17.targetText: The reason the Father loves Me is that I lay down My life in order to take it up again.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("for this reason") points ahead to the ὅτι clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in "The reason … is that".

10:18.sourceText: οὐδεὶς ἦρεν αὐτὴν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ τίθημι αὐτὴν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ. ἐξουσίαν ἔχω θεῖναι αὐτήν, καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω πάλιν λαβεῖν αὐτήν· ταύτην τὴν ἐντολὴν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου.
10:18.targetText: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from My Father.”

groups.note: Same verb, in another form in BSB's Greek text; N1904 ἦρεν means "took".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat "I have" before the second authority.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

10:19.sourceText: Σχίσμα πάλιν ἐγένετο ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους.
10:19.targetText: Again there was division among the Jews because of Jesus’ message.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB says "Jesus’ message" for τοὺς λόγους τούτους ("these words"); the article and the demonstrative are not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker of the words; the Greek has τούτους ("these").

10:20.sourceText: ἔλεγον δὲ πολλοὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν Δαιμόνιον ἔχει καὶ μαίνεται· τί αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε;
10:20.targetText: Many of them said, “He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?”

groups.note: Δαιμόνιον ἔχει ("He has a demon") is rendered He is demon-possessed.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

10:21.sourceText: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα οὐκ ἔστιν δαιμονιζομένου· μὴ δαιμόνιον δύναται τυφλῶν ὀφθαλμοὺς ἀνοῖξαι;
10:21.targetText: But others replied, “These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”

targetPhrases.text: of a man possessed by a demon

groups.note: One genitive participle ("of one who is demon-possessed").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the question particle μή (expecting "no") as a plain question.

unmappedTarget.reason: English marks the contrast; the Greek has no connective here.
English supplies an article before eyes; ὀφθαλμούς has none.
English supplies an article to use blind as a noun; τυφλῶν has none.

10:22.sourceText: Ἐγένετο τότε τὰ ἐνκαίνια ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις· χειμὼν ἦν·

groups.note: τὴν ψυχὴν … αἴρεις ("You lift the soul") is an idiom for keeping someone in suspense.
